note: C6 — request-side attacks. Every other fixture varies what a package SHIPS; these vary what a caller ASKS. The §3.2.1 servable set and §3.2.2 confinement are the newest and most security-sensitive surface in the contract and had no coverage at all: nothing here requires a hostile package, only a hostile request. Each case is a request plus the envelope a conformant surface MUST return.

cases.why: The highest-risk injection surface, refused by name. A surface that serves it has reopened the channel the closed servable set exists to shut.
Free prose is never servable regardless of where it sits. The inventory comes from `list`, composed by the surface.
Fails the single-segment grammar before any path work happens. MUST NOT be normalized into an acceptable form.
An absolute path is not a document name.
Contains a separator, so it fails the grammar — and would escape the root even if it did not. The grammar check is what makes the path check unnecessary here.

The name is whitelisted and passes the grammar; only realpath resolution catches it. This is the case name-string filtering cannot detect, and the reason §3.2.2 binds confinement to the RESOLVED path.
A servable name the package does not ship is ABSENT, not DOCUMENT_NOT_SERVABLE. This is the §3.2.1 correction: list.documents is the input domain, never a precondition.
Resolving a dotted name imports the parent and runs its __init__. The rejection MUST happen before resolution is attempted, which is why §3.0 makes `package` a single segment.
The file exists and does not parse. Reporting it absent would tell a consumer the package ships nothing, which is false and hides a real problem.
Parses as JSON, fails its schema (api_index is a string). §3.2.1 now requires validation before serving, so METADATA_UNREADABLE covers schema-invalidity and not only malformed JSON.
